title: Swe entry scenario duplicate rows join
topic: Swe entry scenario duplicate rows join
question: A report that's supposed to show one row per order is showing some orders two or three times. What's your first guess, and how do you confirm it?
idealAnswer:
Correctly identifies the likely cause: joining a one-to-many relationship (one order, many items) produces one result row per matching item, not per order

Proposes confirming by checking how many item rows exist for one of the duplicated orders, expecting the duplicate count to match the item count

Suggests a fix appropriate to the actual goal: aggregate/group the item data (e.g. GROUP BY order with an aggregate function) if only one row per order is wanted, or accept multiple rows if item-level detail is actually needed

Distinguishes this from a genuine duplicate-data bug, doesn't jump straight to 'there must be duplicate rows in the orders table' without checking the join first

Bonus: mentions counting expected vs actual rows as a general debugging technique for join-related duplication bugs
